title: Imaging-based quantification of RNAPII clearance during transcription-coupled DNA repair
author: de Groot, van der Meer, et al.

steps.title: Remove PBS
steps.instruction: Remove PBS from each coverslip using a pipette or suction system.

steps.title: Permeabilize cells
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of 0.5 % Triton‑X‑100 to each coverslip and incubate 15 min at 18‑22 °C.

steps.title: Block with BSA (first)
steps.instruction: Wash coverslips twice with 1 mL 3 % BSA in PBS, 5 min each, to block non‑specific binding.

steps.title: PBS wash
steps.instruction: Wash once with 1 mL PBS for 5 min.

steps.title: Glycine quench
steps.instruction: Incubate coverslips in 100 mM glycine in PBS for 10 min at 18‑22 °C.

steps.title: Post‑glycine wash
steps.instruction: Wash once with 1 mL PBS for 5 min.

steps.title: DNA denaturation
steps.instruction: Treat cells with 1 mL 0.5 M NaOH in PBS for 5 min, then discard solution immediately.

steps.title: Remove NaOH
steps.instruction: Wash twice with 1 mL PBS, 5 min each, to eliminate residual NaOH.

steps.title: Reduce volume & transfer
steps.instruction: Transfer coverslips with tweezers onto a parafilm‑covered surface, keep them wet with PBS, and limit subsequent wash/block volumes to ~0.3 mL per coverslip.

steps.title: Second BSA block
steps.instruction: Block coverslips with 10 % BSA in PBS for 15 min at 18‑22 °C.

steps.title: Equilibrate in washing buffer
steps.instruction: Incubate coverslips in washing buffer (WB) for 15 min.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Apply 100 µL of primary‑antibody mix (anti‑CPD and anti‑elongating RNAPII) to each coverslip; incubate 2 h at 18‑22 °C or overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Primary antibody washes
steps.instruction: Wash coverslips four times with WB, 5 min each.

steps.title: Secondary antibody + DAPI
steps.instruction: Incubate coverslips with 100 µL secondary‑antibody solution containing DAPI for 1 h in the dark (light‑sensitive reagents).

steps.title: Post‑secondary washes
steps.instruction: Wash once with WB for 5 min, then twice with PBS for 5 min each.

steps.title: Mount in Polymount
steps.instruction: Apply two drops of Polymount per microscope slide, pick up each coverslip with tweezers, tip off excess PBS, place the cell‑side down onto a drop, avoid air bubbles and press lightly if needed.

steps.title: Dry and store
steps.instruction: Dry mounted slides overnight at 18‑22 °C in the dark; store up to 1 week at 4 °C before imaging.

steps.title: Run ImageJ macro
steps.instruction: Open the script “RNAPII_clearance_DataExtraction_ImageJ_DvdH_20250905_final.txt” in ImageJ, select the folder containing 3‑channel stacked .czi files, and run the macro.

substeps.instruction: Use a computer that meets ImageJ minimal requirements.
Ensure images are 3‑channel stacked; only such files are processed.

steps.title: Set macro parameters
steps.instruction: Define nucleus diameter 10‑30 units; set number of channels = 3; nuclei channel = 1 (DAPI), focus channel = 2 (CPD, A488), measurement channel = 3 (RNAPII, A555); minimal focus area = 0; focus threshold = Yen, nucleus threshold = Li; keep other defaults.

steps.title: Generate results file
steps.instruction: After the macro finishes, locate the “_Results_focus analyses” folder containing an Excel file with ROI intensities and background values, plus zipped ROI folders.

steps.title: Map result columns
steps.instruction: Open the results Excel file and note column assignments: A =data point, B =label, C‑I =DAPI damage ROI, J‑N =DAPI undamaged ROI, P‑T =CPD damage ROI, U‑Y =CPD undamaged ROI, AA‑AE =RNAPII damage ROI, AF‑AJ =RNAPII undamaged ROI, O, Z, AK =average background for channels 1‑3.

steps.title: Transfer data to analysis template
steps.instruction: Copy column B to column C of the template and split labels at “.” then “‑” to obtain condition (C) and image number (D); copy RNAPII area (AA) → G, intensity (AB) → H; copy CPD area (P) → F, intensity (Q) → I; copy RNAPII undamaged area (AF) → K, intensity (AG) → L; copy CPD undamaged area (U) → J, intensity (V) → M; copy RNAPII background (AK) → N; fill condition names in the yellow cells starting at AI43.

steps.title: Define ROI size and intensity cut‑offs
steps.instruction: Using the template graphs, set minimum and maximum damaged‑area sizes in cells AG1 and AH1, and CPD intensity limits in AI1 and AJ1, to exclude outlier ROIs; adjust thresholds as needed for the dataset.

steps.title: Calculate ratios and normalize
steps.instruction: The template computes the RNAPII intensity ratio (damage/undamaged) per nucleus, normalizes each value to the 0 h time point (columns CY), and generates summary statistics and plots (e.g., AT63).

steps.title: Plot normalized data
steps.instruction: Export the normalized ratios and plot them with PlotsOfData (https://huygens.science.uva.nl/PlotsOfData/) or equivalent software, following the example shown in Figure 2B.

description: Removal of RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) from DNA after stalling at a transcription-blocking DNA lesion is a crucial step in transcription-coupled repair (TCR). The TCR pathway is initiated when transcribing RNAPII stalls at DNA damage in the template strand, such as cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers (CPDs) caused by ultraviolet (UV) light exposure.2,3 Initially, the sequential and cooperative actions of TCR proteins CSB, CSA, ELOF1, UVSSA and STK19 recruit and position TFIIH onto DNA damage-stalled RNAPII.1,4,5,6,7 The subsequent clearance of RNAPII is required to provide downstream nucleotide excision repair (NER) proteins access to the lesions, enabling dual incision and ultimately repair of the damaged DNA.8,9,10
